title: Introduction + How Make Time Works
coreMove: Name the default force running the day, then choose which part of the Make Time loop will take command first.
sourcePressure: The source sidecar identifies the opening problem as Busy Bandwagon plus Infinity Pools and the answer as the four-part architecture: Highlight, Laser, Energize, Reflect.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The wrong generic version says modern life is distracting and people need better discipline. The specific move is to spot default control and answer it with a deliberate counter-default from the framework.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

counterintuition: productivity is not about doing more
you need discipline less than design
tryThisNow: put your phone away for five minutes

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: a neighborhood film-festival programmer sorting premieres from sponsor demands
exampleSpecs.audience: a cultural organizer whose day gets claimed by visible responsiveness
exampleSpecs.stakes: the opening-night lineup becomes mediocre if sponsor replies consume the screening window
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she writes Busy Bandwagon beside the sponsor reply queue, circles one film reel evaluation as the Highlight, and pins a two-hour screening block above the registration binder
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stack of screeners beside a plastic box of red lanyards at 8:18 a.m.
mustAvoid: email overload as the whole lesson

exampleSpecs.domain: a food-pantry route coordinator preparing a Saturday delivery map
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer lead pulled between urgent texts and route design
exampleSpecs.stakes: three apartment towers miss produce boxes if the route remains improvised
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he labels the group chat an Infinity Pool for the next hour, turns the delivery map face up, and uses Highlight before checking the new message count
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated city map spread under a crate tag marked Building C

exampleSpecs.domain: an aquarium exhibit technician opening a kelp-tank maintenance shift
exampleSpecs.audience: a hands-on specialist whose day can vanish into visitor alerts and repair pings
exampleSpecs.stakes: the pump inspection slips if the first hour becomes scattered response work
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, he follows every alert light; after, he names the alert panel as the day's default and starts the Highlight inspection checklist before Laser limits the pager route
exampleSpecs.firstImage: green tank light rippling across a clipboard clipped to a rail

exampleSpecs.domain: an immigration paralegal preparing asylum exhibits before a filing cutoff
exampleSpecs.audience: a legal support worker stuck between urgent status calls and careful packet assembly
exampleSpecs.stakes: a client's evidence packet may be rejected if the exhibit order is rushed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a day lost to calls, she marks Busy Bandwagon beside the call log and chooses tomorrow's first Make Time move as a protected exhibit-order Highlight
exampleSpecs.firstImage: color-coded exhibit tabs fanned beside a stamped filing receipt

exampleSpecs.domain: an amateur choir director choosing a rehearsal plan for a memorial service
exampleSpecs.audience: a community leader tempted to answer every singer text first
exampleSpecs.stakes: the choir will stumble through the difficult entrance if rehearsal starts without a chosen center
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she tells the section lead that singer texts are the Busy Bandwagon today, then writes one Highlight on the rehearsal folder before touching the message thread
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pencil-marked score open to the first alto entrance

exampleSpecs.domain: a rural vet-clinic receptionist triaging surgery slots and social messages
exampleSpecs.audience: a front-desk operator whose reactive day looks responsible but leaves the real queue untouched
exampleSpecs.stakes: two surgery confirmations drift if the day starts inside the clinic's social feed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she draws two columns labeled Busy Bandwagon and Infinity Pools, places the appointment confirmations under Highlight, and leaves the clinic feed closed until the confirmations are done
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a yellow surgery schedule taped beside a jar of numbered kennel tags

skillTargets: distinguish Busy Bandwagon pressure from Infinity Pool pull in unfamiliar scenes
choose the first framework move after diagnosing a default
explain why trying harder is weaker than redesigning the opening of the day
evaluate whether an action creates leverage or merely adds another productivity ritual

tryThisNowSpec: Look at the next open hour and write one label beside it: Busy Bandwagon, Infinity Pool, or chosen. If it is not chosen, name the first Make Time move that would reclaim it.
